references.geographic_scope: Richards Bay cross section at30S along the main Agulhas Current.
references.temporal_scope: AUCE February–March2003 quasi-synoptic survey; exact cross-section dates not assigned.
references.source_definition: Depth where source-selected section-integrated transport per unit depth reaches zero.
references.qualification: Depth of a laterally integrated transport diagnostic, not a pointwise zero-speed surface or physical lower boundary everywhere. Source eddy cancellation, counterflow exclusions and local section choices matter. Port Shepstone deep barotropic variability may be temporally aliased. The1500–3500m span is spatial, not seasonal extrema or numerical uncertainty.
references.source_locator: Section4.4 paragraph44 and Figure8 for depths; Section4.3 paragraphs39–40 and Figure6 for current definition and section exceptions.

references.source_definition: OSW inferred inclusive reach from visibly nonzero source-labeled Subarctic Current curve at labeled500m in original Figure7b.

records.name: Antarctic Coastal Current (East Wind Drift)

references.geographic_scope: Source section 1: West Antarctic Peninsula continental shelf.
references.temporal_scope: Moving-median composite of disjoint historical seal-profile sampling periods and both source seasons. No dated synoptic section or continuous2005–2015 coverage.
references.source_definition: Source Table2 mean depth of the salinity-selected AACC layer, retaining its same-section spatial depth range.
references.qualification: Mean depth and depth range summarize one non-simultaneous composite section selected by the34.4psu isohaline, not a detected full-flow bottom, uncertainty interval or annual envelope. The400m no-motion reference is a processing choice, not current thickness. Matching width is retained by exact same-source row/operator join; this does not establish section area because the precise mean-depth weighting has not been independently recovered. No rectangular cross-section, dated footprint, along-route profile or volume inferred. Seven sections are spatial cases, not seven independent time repeats. Source Table1 summer dominance in sections1 and6 is retained; section6 conflicts with the prose assertion of winter dominance except section1. Regional coastal current remains distinct from Antarctic Slope Current.
references.source_citation: Schubert, Thompson, Speer, Schulze Chretien and Bebieva(2021), The Antarctic Coastal Current in the Bellingshausen Sea, doi:10.5194/tc-15-4179-2021.
references.source_locator: Final original Table2 printed4189/PDF11 row1; Table1 printed4183/PDF5 row1; methods2.1–2.3 printed4181–4183/PDF3–5.

records.name: East Adriatic Current

references.geographic_scope: NAdEx2015 station A4 off the northeastern Croatian coast, explicitly identified by the authors as sampling the Eastern Adriatic Current rather than channel exchange.
references.temporal_scope: Figure7 observed residual mean over1February–1April2015. Distinct from the full late-November2014–early-July2015 A4 deployment.
references.source_definition: OSW conservative inclusive reach bound from the nonzero observed mean-current vector at the labeled30m depth tick in Figure7 A4 panel.
references.qualification: Figure-presence inference only: read the observed ADCP mean vector, not the standard-deviation ellipse or the blue model set. No arrow-length velocity digitization, speed threshold, significance test, detected terminal boundary or deepest-flow claim. Figure negative vertical-coordinate labels are read as positive depth below the surface.56m is station water depth, not a measured current bottom. A1/A2 channel exchanges and A7–A9 Kvarner circulation are distinct cases. Source model underestimates speeds and is not the basis of this observed bound. Two-month mean does not establish continuous instantaneous reach, seasonal extrema or a route-wide profile.
references.source_citation: Vilibic et al.(2018), Wintertime dynamics in the coastal northeastern Adriatic Sea: the NAdEx2015 experiment, doi:10.5194/os-14-237-2018.
references.source_locator: Figure7 A4 panel, observed ADCP set on left,30m depth tick; caption for averaging period; Section4 A4 paragraph for current identity; Section2.2 for56m station depth and deployment.

references.temporal_scope: August1997 hydrographic section; month precision.
references.source_definition: Observed southwestward coastal jet reported as about100m deep.
references.qualification: Regional snapshot, not entire along-coast depth or seasonal extrema. The160m seabed at nearest approach is separate from100m reported current depth. Distinguish EGCC from the offshore East Greenland Current; no bottom-from-bathymetry or paired whole-flow thickness inferred.
references.source_locator: Primary publisher abstract, Discovery230/A25 August1997 description.

records.name: Guiana Current

references.geographic_scope: French Guiana shelf-edge mooring M2,5deg25.16minN,50deg56.71minW; regional episodic northwestward shelf expression associated with NBC cross-shelf intrusion.
references.temporal_scope: Post-transition northwestward regime within6October2003–18February2004 mooring record. Transition is site/depth dependent between late November and mid-December2003; not year-round flow.
references.source_definition: OSW inferred inclusive reach to the deepest valid M2 ADCP sample118m from the source report that the later northwestward regime occupied the full sampled column.
references.qualification: 118m is the instrument-limited deepest valid sample, not a detected flow bottom or proof of flow below it. Source full-column language is restricted here to the valid13–118m domain; no0–150.3m physical layer,105m thickness or extrapolation to the130m ADCP mounting depth. The early regime oscillated and was not the same northwestward current. The paper challenges a permanent Guyana Current at22m and below; retain episodic identity and regional shelf scope instead of imposing a universal annual current. NBC rings, southeastward Guiana undercurrent and deeper circulation are not assigned this depth. M3 fouling and lost M1 meter are separate instruments, not M2 depth evidence.
references.source_citation: Baklouti, Devenon, Bourret, Froidefond, Ternon and Fuda(2007), New insights in the French Guiana continental shelf circulation and its relation to the North Brazil Current retroflection, doi:10.1029/2006JC003520.
references.source_locator: Abstract for record dates and Guyana-current persistence; Section2 paragraphs10–12/Table1 for M2 and valid13–118m; Section3.1 paragraphs15–16 for regime transition and whole-column northwestward flow.

records.name: Hiri Current

references.geographic_scope: Northward Hiri branch along the Australian coast, connected to the clockwise Gulf of Papua flow; not only the narrow south-PNG naming convention.

references.qualification: Strict lower reach bound for the modeled Australian branch. Does not fix the bottom at300m or apply that depth to the whole PNG arc. records.name: North Pacific Current

references.geographic_scope: Source North Pacific Current distinct from its northern Subarctic/Aleutian Current and the westward Alaskan Stream; undated illustrative geostrophic profile, no exact section coordinates recovered.
references.temporal_scope: Undated historical profile synthesis published1975; not dated to the nearby1955 NORPAC transport table or February Burkov1966 transport chart.
references.source_definition: OSW infers inclusive reach to at least500m from explicit nonzero current speed at500m.
references.qualification: Source states speed at500m is approximately half the surface value and explicitly warns that the ratio varies in space and time.500m is neither the deepest flow nor a terminal boundary, e-folding scale or calibrated whole-route half-speed depth. No exponential profile or depth-to-volume conversion assumed. Unlocated historical source profile remains ineligible for projection onto the catalog NOAA160E–145W reference route. The prose half-speed statement for North Pacific/Alaskan Stream must not be transferred to Subarctic/Aleutian, whose distinct curve is shown without that numerical prose statement.
references.source_citation: Tabata(1975), The general circulation of the Pacific Ocean and a brief account of the oceanographic structure of the North Pacific Ocean, PartI, doi:10.1080/00046973.1975.9648394.
references.source_locator: Section5, printed151/PDF21 first paragraph and Figure7b printed150/PDF20. Section3c printed140–141/PDF10–11 distinguishes current naming.

Thermocline, water-mass core and sampling depth are separate quantities; none supplies another current-bottom measurement.
No reassignment to the regional Ligurian identity and no duplicate count under both identities.
Primary HTML manually reviewed before first retained original-source capture; no original response previously retained in this source case.

references.geographic_scope: Bjørnøya hydrographic section in the source’s broad high-latitude NwASC continuation. No point longitude or exact core-axis position assigned.
references.temporal_scope: 1993–2022 hydrographic/altimetry mean;53 unevenly sampled Bjørnøya transects, with seasonal bias. Static mean mask, not an instantaneous or quarterly depth series.
references.source_definition: Approximate maximum depth of the Atlantic-Water core selected by descending absolute geostrophic velocity until50% of section mean transport is represented.
references.qualification: Maximum static mask depth is not a full-current bottom or uniform thickness.50m is an imposed surface exclusion. Do not inherit Svinøy1500m or Gimsøy2500m lateral cutoff at Bjørnøya; no numerical Bjørnøya isobath cutoff is established. Source mean-mask cell areas slightly overestimate geometric area by ignoring topographic cell cuts. Quarterly interpolation oversamples the sparse section and supplies no seasonal mask-depth data. Source broad NwASC geography may overlap names used for West Spitsbergen flow; no independent duplicate component volume or identity inheritance. BSO uses a different salinity ranking and remains excluded from velocity-ranked core pairing.
references.source_citation: Baumann et al.(2026), Reduced cooling in the Norwegian Atlantic Slope Current, Ocean Science22:17–29, doi:10.5194/os-22-17-2026.
references.source_locator: Section2.1.2 final spatial-extent paragraph and original Figure3d, printed21/PDF5; Section2.1 sampling; Section2.3 source core areas.

records.name: South Atlantic Current

references.geographic_scope: South Atlantic subtropical frontal zone, Cape Basin crossings between15W and5E; two frontal jets associated with NSTF and SSTF.
references.temporal_scope: Multicruise regional synthesis: V2 December1978, AJAX October1983, SAVE4 January1989, Tristan April1989/February1990 and WOCE A11 January1993. Not continuous1978–1993 coverage.
references.source_definition: Approximate lower extent of the layer carrying the source-described dominant flow, not the deepest detected flow.
references.qualification: Primarily in the upper1000m does not quantify a transport fraction, imply zero below1000m, or establish whole-route thickness. The1500m level of no motion is a reconstruction assumption, not a measured current bottom. Between-front flow may reverse; two eastward jets must not be represented as one uniformly filled section. Six Cape Basin cases have uneven support, including limited V2 data below500m and an incompletely crossed northern front in1990. Argentine Basin SAVE5 comparisons and Brazil Current recirculation are not independent confirmation of a uniform route depth. No annual depth extrema inferred.
references.source_citation: Smythe-Wright, Chapman, Duncombe Rae, Shannon and Boswell(1998), Characteristics of the South Atlantic subtropical frontal zone between15W and5E, doi:10.1016/S0967-0637(97)00068-X.
references.source_locator: Section4.4, printed188/PDF21 first paragraph; printed182/PDF16 for1500m geostrophic reference; Section2 printed170/PDF4 and Table1 printed180/PDF14 for cruise scope.

It is not a continuous directly measured velocity layer, a0.5m physical top or15m detected flow bottom, a14.5m thickness, uncertainty or seasonal range. Separate Shelf15–26m, offshore upper-layer and dense NAdDW/ADW waters must not be inherited into the named coastal-current depth. The deeper cascading event motivates the study but does not make WACC a bottom current. No assignment to the2018 publication year or separate model initialization dates.

references.geographic_scope: Southern component of the western/southern Australian boundary system, Cape Leeuwin to Tasmania; southern_Australian_margin. Does not cover the western-coast North West Cape–Cape Leeuwin limb.
references.temporal_scope: Source seasonal regional hydrographic summary; exact contributing occupation dates not recovered from the abstract. Publication2019 is not an observation year.
references.source_definition: Approximate depth of the interface between subtropical Leeuwin-System water and subantarctic water transported by the Flinders Current System.
references.qualification: Water-mass interface is not a directly detected zero-velocity boundary or whole-system thickness. Broad winter/summer summaries are not paired repeated sections, independent repeats, confidence bounds or annual extrema. The150m summer exception belongs to upwelling regions and western Tasmania, not every section. Southern Leeuwin-System component evidence cannot assign a common depth to all5500km or to the separate westward Flinders Current. Catalog defines a continuous winter system; summer values remain conditional seasonal context. No exact route projection or calendar months established. Primary institutional indexed abstract reviewed; original6.56MB PDF listed restricted until2037 and not accessed.
references.source_citation: Richardson, Middleton, Kyser, James and Opdyke(2019), Shallow water masses and their connectivity along the southern Australian continental margin, doi:10.1016/j.dsr.2019.103083.
references.source_locator: Original institutional repository Abstract final interface-depth comparison; first sentences for Cape Leeuwin–Tasmania study scope and STSW transport identity.
